A 33-year-old male visits the physician for a routine physical examination. He reports feeling well and
has no significant medical history or current medications. His vital signs are normal, and the physical
examination reveals no abnormalities. Laboratory tests, including a complete blood count and standard
electrolyte panel, are within normal limits. A urine dipstick test is negative for glucose, but a reducing
substance test of the urine is positive. What is the most appropriate dietary recommendation for this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Limit sodium intake to less than 2 g/day (B) Begin a ketogenic diet (C)
Avoid high-protein diets (D) Reduce intake of simple carbohydrates (E) Follow a low-fat diet (F) No
changes needed (G) Eliminate fructose and sucrose (H) Eliminate galactose from the diet (I) Eliminate
galactose and lactose (J) Restrict lactose-containing foods
 A. Restrict lactose-containing foods
B. Limit sodium intake to less than 2 g/day
C. Eliminate fructose and sucrose
D. No changes needed
E. Begin a ketogenic diet
F. Avoid high-protein diets
G. Eliminate galactose and lactose
H. Eliminate galactose from the diet
I. Follow a low-fat diet
J. Reduce intake of simple carbohydrates
